claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a robust strength–ductility balance across varying temperatures and strain rates.
Strain-induced amorphization at grain boundaries governs the Co-free alloy's dynamic behavior.
Dynamic grain-boundary amorphization transiently refines the microstructure.
The transiently refined or amorphous structure enhances dislocation pinning.
Enhanced dislocation pinning increases strain hardening while maintaining ductility.
The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a solidified single-phase solid solution.
Ultra-high vacuum avoids extrinsic surface effects during the proposed mechanical tests.
The proposed tests vary strain rate from quasi-static to high rate and temperature from cryogenic to elevated conditions.
The applicable regime permits internal kinetic structural changes without full recrystallization or diffusion-driven phase changes.
Ultra-nanocrystalline and/or amorphous grain-boundary layers emerge dynamically during deformation.
Increased strain rates and/or non-ambient temperatures generate local stress concentrations that induce grain-boundary amorphization.
Nanoscale disordered regions offset thermal softening or dynamic instability.
The room-temperature, moderate-strain-rate baseline has a uniform grain structure and typical dislocation-based plasticity.
Higher strain rates or varied temperatures will produce a refined, heterogeneous grain structure with detectable amorphous intergranular films relative to the baseline.
The predicted structural changes will correlate with enhanced strain-hardening rates and comparable ductility.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit the predicted dynamic microstructural changes more distinctly than CoCrFeMnNi under identical conditions.
The mechanism should dominate at intermediate strain rates and at temperatures below those causing diffusion-controlled recrystallization.
The mechanism may cease to dominate when complete recovery or recrystallization occurs or when twinning predominates.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits inverse Hall–Petch behavior associated with a dynamic-amorphization model and formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Failure to observe dynamically formed amorphous or ultra-nanocrystalline grain-boundary regions correlated with enhanced strain hardening would falsify the proposed dominant mechanism.
